For any caller distinct from the transaction origin, C's selfdestruct refund goes to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant diverts it to tx.origin, so for such calls the caller's balance stays zero.

For any owner-initiated self-destruct of c with any transaction origin, c's refund goes to the direct caller (owner), never to tx.origin; the mutant diverts it to tx.origin whenever tx.origin differs from the caller.

For any value sent to the contract, calling sudicideAnyone (by the owner) must destroy the contract and pay its entire balance to the caller (msg.sender); the mutant instead sends the balance to the contract itself, so the caller's balance never increases — violating the payout rule for every positive balance.
Calling sudicideAnyone from an account that is not the contract owner must revert; only the owner may trigger it.
